key_insight: A wind-drift-induced Holmboe instability can evolve from infinitesimal disturbances into finite-amplitude, propagating Stokes-like surface waves under background shear.
engineering_relevance: The results connect wave onset and nonlinear propagation in a framework relevant to physics-based modeling of wind-generated ocean waves.
method: Analyze linear instability of uniform airflow over a finite-thickness, constant-vorticity water layer and deep irrotational water.
Initialize two-phase incompressible Navier–Stokes simulations with the fastest-growing eigenmode.
Compare nonlinear wave spectra and profiles with an exact steady traveling-wave boundary-value formulation.
evidence_signal: Simulated early growth agrees excellently with linear theory, while pre-breaking spectra show carrier-locked bound harmonics and time-averaged wave profiles agree very well with nonlinear theory.
watch_item: The findings concern an idealized shear configuration in a high-Bond-number, low-Froude-number regime; applicability to realistic turbulent seas and breaking requires further validation.
paper_title: Oceanic Surface Waves from Wind-Drift-Layer Instability: Exponential Growth to Finite-Amplitude States
